subject.title: [Feature]: Per-agent cost budget enforcement at the gateway level

question: Should OpenClaw implement native core per-agent spend-budget enforcement, expose only a budget-capable plugin/admission API, or leave this to external/provider-account controls?
rationale: The request crosses config shape, provider dispatch, persistent accounting, concurrency semantics, UX/status surfaces, and the core-vs-plugin boundary, so automation cannot choose the product contract safely.

options.title: Build native core budget admission
options.body: Add opt-in budget config, durable ledger/reservation/refund semantics, pre-dispatch enforcement, receipts, and status/doctor UX in the core/provider dispatch path.

options.title: Expose plugin budget primitives only
options.body: Keep core lean by adding only the missing admission/accounting APIs needed for a plugin or ClawHub extension to enforce spend budgets consistently.

options.title: Defer to external controls
options.body: Close or downscope native enforcement and document provider accounts, proxies, or external billing tools as the supported cost-control path.

recommendation.title: Build native core budget admission
recommendation.body: Add opt-in budget config, durable ledger/reservation/refund semantics, pre-dispatch enforcement, receipts, and status/doctor UX in the core/provider dispatch path.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cost-analysis work and product-boundary ownership signals make this the best available owner for the core-vs-plugin budget decision.
